'''Hans Rudolf Griem''' (October 7, 1928 – October 2, 2019)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11512014.html|title=Griem, Hans R.|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-25}}</ref> was a German-American [[physicist]] who specialized in experimental [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] and spectroscopy.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Griem|first=Hans R.|date=1968|title=Semiempirical Formulas for the Electron-Impact Widths and Shifts of Isolated Ion Lines in Plasmas|journal=Physical Review|volume=165|issue=1|pages=258–266|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.165.258|bibcode=1968PhRv..165..258G}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Griem|first=Hans R.|date=1963|title=Validity of Local Thermal Equilibrium in Plasma Spectroscopy|journal=Physical Review|volume=131|issue=3|pages=1170–1176|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.131.1170|bibcode=1963PhRv..131.1170G}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Griem|first1=Hans R.|last2=Kolb|first2=Alan C.|last3=Shen|first3=K. Y.|date=1959|title=Stark Broadening of Hydrogen Lines in a Plasma|journal=Physical Review|volume=116|issue=1|pages=4–16|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.116.4|bibcode=1959PhRv..116....4G}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Griem|first=Hans R.|date=1962|title=High-Density Corrections in Plasma Spectroscopy|journal=Physical Review|volume=128|issue=3|pages=997–1003|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.128.997|bibcode=1962PhRv..128..997G}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Griem received his doctorate from the [[University of Kiel]] in 1954 and in the same year accepted a [[Fulbright Fellowship]] at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] to work on the physics of the [[upper atmosphere]]. He then returned to the University of Kiel for a two-year appointment dealing with high temperature physics. In 1957, he began working at the University of Maryland, first as an [[assistant professor]] in plasma physics before becoming an [[associate professor]] in 1961 and then [[Professor|full professor]] in 1963. He retired as [[professor emeritus]] in 1994.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1512-hans-r-griem-1928-2019.html|title=Hans R. Griem, 1928-2019 - UMD Physics|website=umdphysics.umd.edu|access-date=2020-02-25}}</ref>

From 1976 to 1994, Griem was a consultant at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" />

== Honors and awards ==
In 1967, Griem was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1967&unit_id=APS&institution=Silver+Spring%2C+Maryland|title=APS Fellow Archive|last=|first=|date=|website=www.aps.org|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-25}}</ref> In 1991, he received the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''his numerous contributions to experimental plasma physics and spectroscopy, particularly in the area of improved diagnostic methods for high temperature plasmas, and for his books on plasma spectroscopy and spectral line broadening in plasmas that have become standard references in the field"''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Griem&first_nm=Hans&year=1991|title=1991 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-25}}</ref>

Griem also received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]], a [[Humboldt Award]] and the [[Williams F. Meggers Award|William F. Meggers Award]] of the Optical Society.<ref name=":1" />
